### 📓 Docs Drift Check
This PR changes **1** package(s): `@objectstack/plugin-auth`, touching **19** documentable anchor(s).

**27** hand-written doc(s) name something this change touched — list omitted above 15 rows. Re-derive on the tree named below: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 82838e83adc6f464d2baef055ff7eed6338243f9`.

⛔ **10** release-owned page(s) also affected — read-only, see AGENTS.md Documentation Guardrails.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **2** name(s) were too generic to anchor anything (single lowercase words)
- the SDK route bridge reached **65** of **247** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **182** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **182**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **59** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **123** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **22** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 82838e83adc6f464d2baef055ff7eed6338243f9` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `840f46189f802a73554c4280c351d3aaa7e483d6` — the merge of head `ffe46dd2f162827bab57520de4e60eecb292ca5b` into base `82838e83adc6f464d2baef055ff7eed6338243f9`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin 840f46189f802a73554c4280c351d3aaa7e483d6 && git checkout 840f46189f802a73554c4280c351d3aaa7e483d6
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin 82838e83adc6f464d2baef055ff7eed6338243f9 ffe46dd2f162827bab57520de4e60eecb292ca5b && git checkout -B drift-repro 82838e83adc6f464d2baef055ff7eed6338243f9 && git merge --no-ff ffe46dd2f162827bab57520de4e60eecb292ca5b

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 82838e83adc6f464d2baef055ff7eed6338243f9
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs 82838e83adc6f464d2baef055ff7eed6338243f9` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `TIER_DEFAULT`
Head-sha: `9f2740eb83a00ca989711ce2b69b48782069511c`
Local-runs: none

### ① Derived judgments

- **Declaration face.** `Clause-②: yes (widening)`: one new optional `AuthManagerOptions` member, `organizationDeleteGate`, and two exported types (`OrganizationDeleteGateRequest`, `OrganizationDeleteGateRefusal`). When it is unset, `assertOrganizationDeletable` runs exactly as before (`if (gate)`), pinned by the CONTROL "with no check set, the same delete goes ahead as before". Nothing accepted before is refused by this package on its own; only a host that opts in refuses. `Metadata-protocol: none`, `patch` for a non-protocol widening: correct.
- **Placement.** The gate is asked last, after the mount gates (IP allow-list, one-account), the vendor-mirroring early returns (no session, not a member, no `organization: ['delete']`, no such organization) and the platform's own 403/409/503, and before better-auth's first write. Each placement claim is pinned (IP allow-list never reaches it; 401/409 never reach it; 415 for unparsed bodies; once per delete with the parsed id).
- **Fail-closed.** A throw, or an answer that is not `undefined`/`null`/a well-formed refusal (status an integer 400–499, non-empty `body.code` and `body.message`, `userMessage` a string if present), answers `503` with `ORGANIZATION_DELETE_READ_FAULT_CODE`. The message names the option and never the host's text, which rides `cause`. A well-formed refusal is answered with its own status and body. Pinned per malformed case.
- **Read per call.** A getter over `this.config.organizationDeleteGate`, so `updateConfig` / `auth:configure` take effect. Same pattern as the neighbouring getters.
- nit N1: `if (!engine) return;` at the top of `assertOrganizationDeletable` skips the host gate too when no `dataEngine` is wired. That is the in-memory, non-production path (`createDatabaseConfig` warns), so it is not a hole in a real deployment. The jsdoc's "called once per delete" could still say "when a data engine is wired", or the gate could be hoisted above that return; it doesn't need the engine.
- nit N2: the host's refusal body is passed through as given, including any extra fields. That is right for a trusted host option. The ADR-0112 `code` shape is enforced only as a non-empty string, so a host could answer a code outside the catalog. That's acceptable; the cloud side owns its codes.

### ② Semver level

`@objectstack/plugin-auth: patch` with `Clause-②: yes (widening)`, per AGENTS.md ("a non-protocol change, widening or breaking, ships `patch`"). No spec member moves.

### ③ Boundary flags

- Consumer is the cloud control plane (subscription / remaining environments). The changeset notes that a host body reader ahead of the mount can be dropped. That cloud change is out of this repo and is the follow-up for whoever owns cloud#.
- Docs: `content/docs/permissions/authentication.mdx` gains the option.
- CI at this head when read (16:54Z): 19 success, 15 skipped, 16 in progress, none red. The ACCEPT re-reads every check at the landing head.
